card.name: Words leading up to benefit/risk wording
card.fires_on: Words in a sentence that is about to name benefits, harms or risks, such as 'potential' before 'benefits' or 'hazards to' before the fetus. It also fires on the benefit/risk ratio and on phrases like 'where serious damage would be'.

modes.label: Benefit-risk weighing
modes.description: Words inside or just before a statement that benefits are weighed against hazards or risks.
modes.example: the possible hazards should be weighed against the<< potential>> benefits when administering this drug

modes.label: Inside benefit/risk ratio
modes.description: Partway through the word risk in a benefit/risk ratio.
modes.example: An assessment of benefit/r<<isk>> ratio is recommended to justify use

modes.label: General benefit or harm clauses
modes.description: Words in ordinary text where benefits or damage are being discussed.
modes.example: where the benefits are widespread and where no<< private>>-sector entities are willing to make the investments

card.writes: It lowers the chance that the next word is benefit or harm words, as if those words were already used nearby.
card.plain: It marks the spot in a sentence where benefits and risks are being weighed against each other.
